content.content:
Discarding an open draft ends the draft without landing it. A draft's record has exactly two states — `open` for a draft that has not landed and `landed` for one that has — and the only transition between them is `open` → `landed`, made at the landing itself (vkkwusty). A discard makes no such transition: the landing that would carry the draft to `landed` does not happen, so the discarded draft never reaches the landed end and never will. Nor does it become some third kind of thing, because there is no third state to become: the record is absent from the store, and absence is not a state standing beside `open` and `landed` (vkkwusty, twpvqstu). So the end means exactly this — at the open end, with no landing behind it, the draft stops being a draft that can land.

Only an open draft can be discarded, and a landed record is never discarded. `landed` is terminal — there is nowhere for it to go (vkkwusty) — and the store takes nothing away at the landed end, where a landed record is retained at its handle (twpvqstu). A discard therefore has no purchase there: the draft it ends is one whose landing has not happened. The two states bound the end exactly, one on each side: an open draft is the only subject, and the landed end is untouched. That is the lifecycle read at the end where a draft can still be given up, not a second rule laid beside it.

A discarded draft is never later landed. Landing is per draft (znskspqs), and it is the record for that draft that turns at the landing (vkkwusty); the discarded draft has no record left to turn, and a later attempt at the same work arrives as a new draft with its own record and its own handle (owyntkvw, vkkwusty), to land or be discarded on its own account. Nothing is reopened, because nothing of the discarded draft remains to reopen.

A discard ends one draft, not an edit and not a node. A draft names exactly one node and one edit, is written in its own workspace, and several drafts may name one node — competing alternatives, or a redraft beside an open draft (znskspqs). The end falls on the one draft whose record it is (owyntkvw), so the drafts beside it are not ended with it, and the node and the edit are untouched by it: the draft never landed, so nothing of it was ever recorded into the node's change (znskspqs, vkkwusty). Which record leaves is the store's removal to say, and it takes the document of that one draft (twpvqstu).

What becomes of the record is the store's removal, already decided and relied on here rather than restated. A discarded draft's document leaves, every other record stays at its handle, and a scan afterwards finds the remaining records and not the discarded one; that path, that discovery and that retention are twpvqstu's, recorded there and taken as given (twpvqstu, vkkwusty). What this node settles is the event that removal presupposes — the end of an open draft that will not land — and it adds no step to the removal, moves no document, and says nothing about how the store is read or written.

Discarding is not one of the three operations. An operation is one whole creation, one whole recording, or one whole removal, and only those three bracket (lmwpuqlx, qvkuluyw). A discard is none of them: it creates no node and no change, records no edit into a node, and removes no change. The draft it ends was never a graph node, and its record is neither a node document nor attributed to a change (znskspqs, owyntkvw); the only change a discard makes is in the registry — the record of a draft that will not land leaves it — and a registry write is none of the three (qvkuluyw). The exclusion is not a fourth operation made up for discard; it is the existing vocabulary read against what a discard touches, a draft's record, which the vocabulary never reaches.

The end is never bracketed, and no marker is written for it. The marker stack is one file belonging to the trunk workspace, and draft workspaces neither read nor write it (uqqswnsy); only creation, recording and removal invocations bracket (qvkuluyw), and a discard is none of them. So a discard opens no bracket and closes none, leaves the stack exactly as it stands, and writes no marker anywhere — not in the trunk, and not a per-draft stack of its own (uqqswnsy). There is no bracket to place because there is no operation to bracket.

Undo and redo have no unit to step for a discard. Undo and redo step whole operations, and a registry write is not one (qvkuluyw), so a discard is neither a thing undo reverses nor a thing redo re-applies: it offers them no operation, and it leaves no marker entry for either to move over (qvkuluyw, uqqswnsy). The recording that did land a draft remains the unit undo and redo step (qvkuluyw); a discard never enters that history. Silence there is not a gap to be filled — it is `not an operation` read at the history.

A draft need not be intact for its discard to end it, and a discard is not a repair of drift. Drift is an open record whose workspace jj no longer has, and reconcile reports that difference and changes nothing — it never repairs, rewrites, drops or forgets the record (vuopwuyo). A discard is a different act: what is discarded is the draft the registry holds open (owyntkvw, vkkwusty), and the end is that record leaving by the store's removal (twpvqstu). A drifted draft is still an open draft the registry holds, so ending it is a discard like any other, and the registry then holds no open record of it, but nothing here makes reconcile repair anything: reconcile reports the disagreement and leaves the record standing, while a discard ends the draft (vuopwuyo).

A discard clears the open-draft state that the removal guard reads. `deccy remove <id>` refuses while any open record names the node, naming each such draft by its handle, and a landed record does not block (tzlumxvt). A discarded draft leaves no open record naming its node, so the guard is not answered by that draft — that follows from the removal the store already performs (twpvqstu) and the state filter the guard already applies (tzlumxvt). Nothing about the guard itself changes here: the precondition, the order in which it is asked and the way it names drafts stay exactly as recorded.

These clauses are one commitment, not several. `Ends without landing` is the lifecycle read at the open end (vkkwusty); `only an open draft` is the same statement from the landed end, which is terminal and retained (vkkwusty, twpvqstu); `one draft` is that statement applied to the draft the record identifies rather than to the node, the edit or the drafts beside it (znskspqs, owyntkvw); `not an operation` is the operation vocabulary read against what a discard touches, a draft's record rather than a node or a change (lmwpuqlx, qvkuluyw, owyntkvw); and `never bracketed, no undo unit` is what that exclusion means at the marker stack and at the history (uqqswnsy, qvkuluyw). Take away the end and a discard would be the removal of something that is not a change; take away the open bound and it would reach the landed record that retention keeps; take away the exclusion and the end would have to be one of the three, would bracket, and would offer undo a unit — which would make ending a draft a mutating operation on the graph, the opposite of `without landing`. The clauses hold together or not at all.

Not settled here. The verb surface — the command, its name, flags, arguments, output, refusal wording and exit status — is another commitment. So are the workspace and change mechanics of a discarded draft: whether or how its jj workspace or its change is forgotten, abandoned or otherwise altered. So is the store's removal as twpvqstu records it — the one document, its path, the scan and the retention — which is relied on and not re-decided. So is the removal guard's own rule and ordering (tzlumxvt), and what reconcile reports (vuopwuyo). This node fixes only what a discard is: the end of an open draft, at the open end, without landing, and outside the operation vocabulary.
content.rationale:
This decision is prose because the commitment is what a discard is, and every prerequisite that grounds it is prose: each edge is a natural-to-natural reading, answered by reading the clauses against the recorded prerequisites rather than by any behavior probe.

The node takes the record's lifetime as given and states only its open end. A record has exactly two states and one transition, and `landed` is terminal and retained (vkkwusty); the store already says that a discarded draft's document leaves while a landed one stays at its handle (twpvqstu). What is left is the event those clauses presuppose: what a discard is. It is the end of an open draft that did not land, which is why it can never touch the landed end, and why the ended draft never arrives there and is never reopened.

The operation half is derived, not added beside the rest. An operation is one whole creation, recording or removal (lmwpuqlx); only those bracket, and a registry write is none of the three and gives undo and redo no unit (qvkuluyw). A draft is not a node, and its record is neither a node document nor attributed to a change (znskspqs, owyntkvw), so a discard creates no node and no change, records no edit into one, and removes no change; the only thing it touches is the registry. That one observation yields both remaining clauses: no bracket, because only operations bracket (qvkuluyw) and the stack belongs to the trunk's operations (uqqswnsy); and no undo or redo unit, because undo and redo step whole operations (qvkuluyw).

The clauses that could look like separate rules are the same statement read where else it is asked. Drift is an open record whose workspace is gone, and reconcile only reports it and never repairs it (vuopwuyo), so saying that a drifted draft can still be discarded, and that this is not a repair, is the ownership split read at the end rather than a reconcile policy. The removal guard refuses on open records (tzlumxvt), so saying that a discard stops blocking a removal is the guard's own state filter read after the store's removal (twpvqstu), not a change to the guard. And the record's fate is not re-settled: the document's path, the scan and the retention are twpvqstu's, and this node only names the end that removal presupposes.

Deliberately not here: the verb surface (command, name, flags, arguments, output, refusal wording, exit status); the workspace and change mechanics of a discarded draft (whether or how its jj workspace or its change is forgotten, abandoned or altered); the store's removal path, scan and retention (twpvqstu); the guard's rule and ordering (tzlumxvt); and what reconcile reports (vuopwuyo). Each of those can be decided, changed or dropped without touching what this node settles, and each belongs to a commitment recorded or planned elsewhere.
